Create a Shiny app with a plumber API mounted inside it

Source: R/app.R
spigot_app.Rd

The API is served by the same process, origin and port as the app, under prefix. The pages are served at their paths, static directories at theirs, and every other path is handled by Shiny as usual (www/ files, for an app directory).

Usage

spigot_app(
  pages,
  server = NULL,
  api,
  prefix = "/api",
  require_session = TRUE,
  max_request_size = NULL,
  blueprints = NULL,
  templates = NULL,
  partials = NULL,
  static = NULL,
  root = "."
)

Arguments

pages

One page, served at /, or a named list of pages keyed by path. See the Pages section.

server

Optional Shiny server function.

api

A plumber router or the path to a plumber file, relative to root. A file is read with spigot_api(); a router is used as given, so build it from spigot_api() to get spigot_json() responses. Blueprint APIs are mounted on it.

prefix

URL path the API is mounted under.

require_session

If TRUE, API requests must carry the token of a live session of this app. If FALSE, requests without one still reach the endpoint, where spigot_session() returns NULL.

max_request_size

Largest request body in bytes, applied as options(shiny.maxRequestSize) while the app runs (it also limits shiny::fileInput() uploads). Inf removes the limit. NULL leaves the option as it is.

blueprints

NULL, or a list of spigot_blueprint()s named by the prefix each is served under. See the Blueprints section.

templates

Where spigot_page() template files are looked up, in order: directories, or files matched by their name. A name not found there is a path relative to root. NULL looks only there.

partials

Partials every page can use: a directory, holding one partial per file named by the file name without its extension (nav.html is {{> nav}}), or a named list like spigot_page()'s. A page's own partials win over these.

static

Directories of files to serve as they are: one directory, served at /static, or a named list of them, served at /<name> each. NULL serves none. See the Files section.

root

The directory that relative api, templates, partials and static paths, and template file names not on the search path, are relative to, for the app and its blueprints. A relative root is relative to the working directory when spigot_app() is called.

Value

A shiny.appobj.

Pages

pages is one page, served at /, or a named list of them, such as list("/" = home, "/about" = about, "/docs/intro" = intro). A path is / or one or more segments, not under the API prefix. Relative URLs in every page resolve from the app's root (see spigot_page()). /about/ redirects to /about, and any other path that is not a page or a file gets a 404 HTML page. Only GET requests reach a page.

A page is usually a spigot_page(): a hand-written HTML template. A top-level page (/, /about) can also be anything shiny::shinyApp() accepts as ui, such as shiny::fluidPage(), an shiny::htmlTemplate() document, or a function(req) returning one of those (or an shiny::httpResponse()). Below the top level, pages must be spigot_page()s.

Sessions

Each browser tab is a Shiny session. Its page sends the session token (Shiny.shinyapp.config.sessionId, available once the shiny:sessioninitialized event has fired) in an X-Spigot-Session header, and spigot binds the request to that session; endpoints read it with spigot_session(). A token stops working as soon as its session ends.

With require_session = TRUE, API requests without a live session's token get a 401 JSON response, {"error": "session required", "hint": "..."}, so only open pages of this app can call the API. The hint points at require_session = FALSE.

API requests whose Origin header (or, without one, Referer) names another host than the request's Host (or X-Forwarded-Host) get a 403 JSON response, whatever require_session is.

The browser client

Every page gets spigot.js (see spigot_dependency()), which defines spigot.get(), spigot.post() and friends. They send the session token for you, so a page's own code calls the API with await spigot.get("items", {page: 2}).

Request size

Shiny rejects request bodies larger than getOption("shiny.maxRequestSize") (5 MB by default) before any R handler runs. That response is Shiny's own: status 413 with the plain-text body Maximum upload size exceeded, not JSON. Clients should not assume every error body is JSON.

Blueprints

blueprints is a list of spigot_blueprint()s named by prefix, such as list("/cars" = cars). Each blueprint's pages are served under its prefix, its API under the app's prefix (/api/cars/...), and its static directory at <prefix>/static. Its pages are checked like the app's own: a path served twice, a page under the API prefix or a static path, and a missing template are errors when the app is built.

Files

Files that pages load (scripts, stylesheets, images) can come from two places. www/ is Shiny's: its files are served at the top level (www/app.js at /app.js), and only when the app directory is run (see "Running the app").

static is spigot's, and is served however the app is run. It is one directory, served at /static, or a named list of directories served at /<name> each, such as list(js = "js", img = "assets/img"). A relative directory is relative to root, and a relative root to the working directory when spigot_app() is called. Files are served by httpuv without running R. A name must be one URL segment, other than session, shared and the first segment of prefix, and no page may be at or under a static path.

Pages below the top level get a <base href> to the app's root, so <script src="static/app.js"> loads the same file from every page.

Running the app

Run an app directory: shiny::runApp("myapp") or runApp("myapp/app.R"), as RStudio's Run App button, Shiny Server and Posit Connect do. Shiny loads the files in R/, then sources app.R with the directory as the working directory, serves www/, and keeps that working directory while the app runs.

Printing the object spigot_app() returns also runs the app (at the console, when app.R is sourced with echo, or with Rscript app.R), but Shiny then does none of that. Template and plumber file paths are relative to whatever the working directory is, www/ files get the 404 HTML page (so a browser refuses to run a www/ script), and endpoints can't call functions from R/. static directories are still served. From a terminal, use Rscript -e 'shiny::runApp("myapp")'.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
api <- spigot_api() |> plumber::pr_get("/hello", function() list(msg = "hi"))
home <- spigot_page("<html><head></head><body><p id='msg'></p></body></html>")
shiny::runApp(spigot_app(pages = home, api = api))
} # }
